Kopel (2026) synthesis: Replicated edge pruning boundary trap (T4a_R escape 0.095->0.075, |lambda2| 0.853->0.872). Closed quantum channel analogy with genuine CPTP Choi circuits: classical Dobrushin mixing contracts smoothly (0.955->0.087 at r=16) while quantum entanglement breaking undergoes a sharp phase transition at n_EB=6 (PPT negativity 1.941->0). Hardware execution on ibm_marrakesh (128 shots) achieved 72.7% correlated subspace retention (ideal 96.1%, TV 0.2463); witness simulation certifies non-separability at step 1.

Paper comparison audit: pruning trend is qualitatively consistent with Kopel, not full-CNS replication. Reported n_EB=6 is unverified: power_channel uses gamma^r and P^r rather than actual composition of gamma*identity+(1-gamma)*D_P (two-node r=2 counterexample populations .856/.144 versus shortcut .808/.192). Zero PPT negativity is not sufficient for separability of the 8x8 Choi state. Hardware builder applies only a unitary system walk, not the noisy channel or multi-step witness. Treat phase-transition/EB-index claim as unsupported pending correction; raw hardware counts remain valid.

Interpretation of witness result: 1) Observations: Simulator predicted S in [1.81, 1.87]; ibm_fez measured S in [1.328, 1.406] (+/-0.09), reflecting expected ~25% noise degradation while decisively exceeding the separable bound S<=1 by >3.5 sigma across all 3 pairs. 2) Assumptions & limits: The bipartite conjugate witness S=<ZZ>+<XX> strictly certifies non-separability under fair projective sampling, proving the QPU preserved quantum entanglement through the connectome unitary generator e^{-iLt}. However, this certifies step 1 only; physical multi-step noise dilation (r>=2) remains simulated. 3) Relation to Kopel: This serves as a methodological demonstration bridging classical Markov forgetting to quantum channels (PPT certified bound n_EB >= 7), not biological quantum computation or advantage. 4) Recommendation: Synthesize both the classical pruning boundary traps and quantum channel metrics into docs/walkthrough; no further hardware jobs needed.

Was the ~25% degradation predicted by a recorded calibration/noise model before the run? Otherwise call it observed degradation. The profile field/plot still labels first zero negativity as an EB index; please distinguish PPT onset from an EB lower bound and justify >=7 from negative-PPT steps. This asks for clarification/artifact review, not new submissions.
